items.label: f05-ensurecreated-tradeoff
items.front: ADR 0001: what does SQLite with EnsureCreated (no migrations) buy Atlas, and what does it give up?
items.back: Gains: zero setup (dotnet run/test need no installed services; resetting dev data is deleting atlas.db; each test fixture holds its own in-memory connection open) and tests that run real SQL (unique indexes, FKs, concurrency tokens) instead of the EF in-memory provider's approximations. Cost: no migration history, so a schema change means recreating the database; a production deployment would move to migrations and likely PostgreSQL.

items.label: f08-report-boundaries
items.front: ADR 0010: how are report responsibilities split between ReportEndpoints and ReportService?
items.back: ReportEndpoints keeps authorization and binding and validates query inputs before any arithmetic; optional dates are resolved with TimeProvider and passed, with cancellation, as explicit values into an API-local ReportService, which uses read-only projections for payroll costs and invoice aging. DTO names and JSON shapes stay the same, and no interface is added just to mirror the one implementation.

items.label: f07-request-correlation
items.front: ADR 0011: how does Atlas connect a caller's error to a log line, and what is that mechanism not?
items.back: The server request id is sent as the X-Request-Id header, carried in ProblemDetails as traceId, and written in the completion log; request logging sits outside error handling so the log records the final status of handled failures. It is request correlation, not end-to-end distributed tracing, and secrets and payloads stay out of the request logs.

items.label: f03-version-token
items.front: How Atlas detects a lost update (ADR 0007)?
items.back: IVersioned entities carry a plain int Version, registered as an EF concurrency token for every implementing entity. A stale write, one whose row's Version changed after the entity was loaded, throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException, and a single global ConcurrencyExceptionHandler decides what the caller is told, so no endpoint handles the conflict itself.

items.label: f06-live-vs-ready
items.front: ADR 0011: what do /health, /health/live and /health/ready each check, and why add a live probe?
items.back: /health is preserved and still includes database connectivity; /health/live has no dependency checks; /health/ready runs the checks tagged ready, today database connectivity only. All three are anonymous. Reason: a restart probe on a database-checking endpoint could restart a perfectly responsive process during a dependency outage.

items.label: f09-projection-and-tracking
items.front: Learning note 04: what do Select, Include, tracking and AsNoTracking each contribute to a report query?
items.back: Select projects only the columns needed (a navigation value such as a run's year and month can be projected without loading the full entity); Include loads related entities; tracking lets EF detect changes for SaveChanges, which a report does not need. A scalar projection already avoids tracking, and an explicit AsNoTracking also communicates the read-only intent.

items.label: f04-payroll-snapshot
items.front: ADR 0008: what creating vs completing a PayrollRun does.
items.back: Create (per country + month, platform admin): computes and stores every Payslip and marks expenses Reimbursed in the same unit of work. Complete (one-way Draft -> Completed): one invoice per client, fee on gross only, FX at the period rate; a missing FX rate fails with 409 and leaves it draft.

items.label: f11-fixed-clock
items.front: Lesson 1: what does BootcampApiFactory's fixed clock replace in the birth-date tests, and what stays real?
items.back: It supplies a fixed 1 September 2026 so the tests prove 1 September is allowed and 2 September rejected on any day they run. It replaces only the external time dependency: the production handler still runs the real date comparison, and the tests still call the HTTP endpoint and inspect persistence. Avoid computing "tomorrow" once from the real clock.

items.label: f10-index-evidence
items.front: Learning note 04: what evidence backs a claim that an index makes a query faster, and what does the index cost?
items.back: Inspect the SQL (EF logging or ToQueryString), noting filters, joins, selected columns, ordering and rows returned; compare the query plan before and after on representative data and report the dataset size. An index helps particular lookups but adds storage and write work, and its existence alone does not prove a query uses it.

items.label: f01-round-once
items.front: ADR 0005: the rounding rule, worked through payroll and final pay?
items.back: Round once per component, then derive the rest by arithmetic. Payroll: employer cost and deductions are the rounded products; net = gross - deductions and total cost = gross + employer cost, so net + deductions == gross holds exactly. Final pay: the daily rate is rounded once, then multiplied by the days.

items.label: f12-note-authorship
items.front: Lesson 3: where do a contract note's author and timestamp come from, and does adding a note change Contract.Version?
items.back: The author is the authenticated principal and the timestamp comes from the clock; the body carries only the note text, so a body naming another author is ignored. Appending a note leaves Contract.Version unchanged: a general note alters neither employment terms nor the contract lifecycle. Notes are visible to client viewers and have no API edit or delete routes.

items.label: f02-status-matrix
items.front: ADR 0003: when does a client admin key get 403, and what guards each load?
items.back: Two 403 cases for a client admin: calling a platform-only endpoint, and writing to a different client's id passed in a request body. Every resource load goes through CanViewClient, and every endpoint applies the same matrix uniformly.

items.prompt: A batch request asks to complete two onboarding checklist items, and the second item belongs to a different contract. Per Lesson 3, what gets saved?

choices.text: Both items, as parent membership is checked once the save is done
The first item, as each item is validated and then saved in turn
Neither item, as every item is checked before any box is ticked
The first item, with the response listing the second as rejected

choices: Both items, as parent membership is checked once the save is done
The first item, as each item is validated and then saved in turn
Neither item, as every item is checked before any box is ticked
The first item, with the response listing the second as rejected

items.explanation: Lesson 3 lines 9-16: the batch endpoint first checks the entire request (permission, item count, duplicate IDs, note lengths, parent membership, versions and completion state) and only then changes the validated items and saves them together. A loop that validates and saves one item at a time could leave the first item complete when the second fails, which the two-phase design exists to prevent; nothing is partly applied.

items.prompt: An amendment raising a salary is approved with an EffectiveDate of 15 May. What salary does May's payroll use?

The new salary for the whole of May, with no proration by day

The old salary; a raise starts in the first full month after it

The new salary for the whole of May, with no proration by day
The old salary to 14 May and the new one after, prorated by days
The old salary; a raise starts in the first full month after it

items.explanation: EffectiveForMonth takes the latest record with EffectiveDate on or before the month end, so the 15 May record wins for May. The ADR documents the simplification: a mid-month change owns that whole month. There is no proration, no full-month delay, and no averaging; LastOrDefault picks one record.

One catches staleness at load time, the other changes made after it
The WHERE clause suffices, and the early check only speeds up tests
The early check suffices, and the WHERE clause only feeds logging

items.explanation: Lesson 3 line 53: the early expected-version check gives a clear failure when a request is already stale at load time, and the database condition (UPDATE ... WHERE Version = original, lines 41-49) catches changes that happen after that check. You need both because they operate at different moments; neither one alone covers both windows, and neither is a duplicate kept for safety.

items.prompt: Two callers load the same pending leave request and both approve it. The second SaveChanges finds the Version changed. What does that caller get?

A 412 Precondition Failed, since it sent no If-Match header

A 200, and its decision quietly overwrites the first approval
A 500 error, because nothing maps DbUpdateConcurrencyException

items.explanation: ConcurrencyExceptionHandler recognises the write conflict and writes a 409 problem body ("Reload it and retry"). Lost updates are what the token prevents, Atlas uses no ETag preconditions, and the global handler is exactly what keeps this from being a 500.

items.prompt: A contract status filter receives the text `999`, and the enum declares only Draft, Active and Terminated. What does Lesson 1 say Enum.TryParse on its own does with that text?

choices.text: It parses it, which is why the rule adds an Enum.IsDefined check
It parses it only if the enum carries the [Flags] attribute
It returns false, as 999 matches none of the members declared
It maps 999 to the nearest declared member, here Terminated

choices: It parses it, which is why the rule adds an Enum.IsDefined check
It parses it only if the enum carries the [Flags] attribute
It returns false, as 999 matches none of the members declared
It maps 999 to the nearest declared member, here Terminated

items.explanation: Lesson 1 lines 66-68: TryParse answers whether text converts to the enum's underlying representation, and it can successfully parse 999 even when the enum declares only Draft, Active and Terminated. The shared defined-enum rule therefore checks parsing and Enum.IsDefined, and also rejects comma-separated combinations because these filters accept one value, not a flags expression. Nothing maps a number to a nearest member.

items.prompt: Headcount is requested with a PH filter. A shortcut builds the full report and then removes the non-PH entries from the final country array. What does Lesson 1 say goes wrong?

The country rows go missing while the totals stay correct
The total and client breakdown still describe every country

items.explanation: Lesson 1 lines 120-122: the service applies the optional filter before selecting and grouping records, so the total, the country breakdown and the client breakdown all describe the same PH population. Filtering the final country array alone would leave a misleading overall total and client breakdown, which is why the test checks the sum of client counts as well as the visible country rows.

items.prompt: What does PayrollCalculator.RoundMoney(2.345m) return?

choices.text: 2.34, because a midpoint is rounded to the even digit
2.35, because a midpoint is rounded away from zero
2.34, since decimal amounts are truncated, not rounded
2.345, since RoundMoney keeps three places for FX

choices: 2.34, because a midpoint is rounded to the even digit
2.35, because a midpoint is rounded away from zero
2.34, since decimal amounts are truncated, not rounded
2.345, since RoundMoney keeps three places for FX

items.explanation: RoundMoney is Math.Round(amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero), so 2.345 goes to 2.35. Round-to-even (banker's rounding, the .NET default) would give 2.34; the ADR rejects it. RoundMoney always rounds to 2 places, and it rounds rather than truncates.

items.prompt: An admin deactivates a client's API key. When does that key stop working?

choices.text: When its issued JWT expires, after the five-minute skew
After an in-memory key cache refreshes, about hourly
Only once the ApiUser row is deleted from the table

Only once the ApiUser row is deleted from the table
On its next request, as every request looks up ApiUsers

items.explanation: HandleAuthenticateAsync queries ApiUsers on every request and fails when !user.IsActive, so revocation is immediate. Atlas issues no JWTs (the ADR lists that as avoided infrastructure), there is no key cache, and keys are revoked by deactivation precisely so rows are never deleted.

The template is configuration and the rows are copied work, so a contract created yesterday keeps yesterday's title and one created tomorrow receives the new title. Rows do not reuse template item IDs, and neither a version bump nor a read re-applies the template.

items.prompt: Country creation trims the name and rejects a 101-character name with a field-specific 400. A reviewer proposes deleting that check because the entity already carries an EF maximum-length annotation. What does Lesson 1 say?

Keep it, but run it after saving so the constraint gets the first say

items.explanation: Lesson 1 lines 47-52 name two separate responsibilities: API validation gives the user a useful error and refuses values outside the documented contract, while database constraints protect stored relationships and uniqueness even for writers other than this endpoint. An EF maximum-length annotation is not a substitute for the first, especially with SQLite. Validation happens before saving, and the test checks both the 400 and the absence of the rejected row.

items.prompt: BenefitPlan computes EmployerShare as RoundMoney(MonthlyCost * EmployerContributionRate). How is EmployeeShare computed?

MonthlyCost - EmployerShare, so both shares re-add to the cent
RoundMoney(MonthlyCost * (1 - rate)), rounded on its own
MonthlyCost times the rate, truncated toward zero at two places

items.explanation: BenefitPlan.cs line 42: EmployeeShare => MonthlyCost - EmployerShare. The remainder is never rounded independently, which is why the split always re-adds to the premium. Rounding both sides separately is the drift the ADR forbids, and Atlas uses one AwayFromZero rounding, never banker's rounding or truncation.

items.prompt: A worker list sorts by name and then Id, and several workers share a name. A refactor swaps `.ThenBy(w => w.Id)` for a second `.OrderBy(w => w.Id)`. What changes, per Lesson 1?

items.explanation: Lesson 1 line 96: a name is not a unique sort key, so the implementation sorts by name, then Id. ThenBy extends an order; a second OrderBy would replace the first order, leaving the list ordered by Id alone. Names are not made unique (line 100 warns against hiding a query-design issue that way), and the lesson describes the second OrderBy as replacing the order, not as an error.

A stronger guarantee may need a shared balance/version row, suitable isolation or another database-backed coordination policy. The version check catches decisions made on stale loaded state (line 9); it does not serialize inserts or turn this into a 409.

items.explanation: Lesson 1 lines 74-82: omitted, true and false are three inputs (do not filter, active countries, inactive countries). A condition that runs only when the value is true loses the false case: false skips the filter and behaves like omitted. The fix checks whether a value was supplied and compares to it, and the currencyCode=USD&isActive=false test proves both filters stay active even when the expected result is empty.

items.prompt: The invoice list is filtered with payrollRunId set to a well-formed GUID that matches no payroll run. Per Lesson 1, what does the caller get?

choices.text: An empty matching collection, with the GUID accepted as valid
A database error, raised when the foreign key lookup finds no run
A binding error, as for any GUID text that names no stored row
A 404, the same as a detail route asked for a missing document

choices: An empty matching collection, with the GUID accepted as valid
A database error, raised when the foreign key lookup finds no run
A binding error, as for any GUID text that names no stored row
A 404, the same as a detail route asked for a missing document

items.explanation: Lesson 1 line 62: the payrollRunId filter accepts a syntactically valid GUID even if no such run exists, and then returns an empty matching collection. A binding error is reserved for malformed GUID text, a 404 is what a detail route returns when one document is missing, and neither case is a database crash.

items.prompt: Why does AtlasDbContext convert every DateTimeOffset to a long instead of keeping EF Core's default SQLite mapping?

choices.text: Integers take less disk space, which is the main concern of the ADR
The default stores local time, so two servers would disagree on it
The default is TEXT, which SQLite cannot compare as instants
SQLite rejects DateTimeOffset columns, so EnsureCreated would fail

choices: Integers take less disk space, which is the main concern of the ADR
The default stores local time, so two servers would disagree on it
The default is TEXT, which SQLite cannot compare as instants
SQLite rejects DateTimeOffset columns, so EnsureCreated would fail

items.explanation: ADR 0004: SQLite has no date-time type, EF stores DateTimeOffset as TEXT, and ORDER BY or range filters on those strings get wrong semantics or client evaluation. Table creation works fine with TEXT, size is never mentioned, and the issue is comparison, not local time.

items.prompt: A contract-creation request reads "country active" while another request pauses hiring in that country. How does Lesson 3 stop the creation from saving on its stale observation?

choices.text: Creation also touches Country.Version, so the stale writer conflicts
The pause cancels in-flight creations by deleting their drafts
Creation re-reads the country inside a lock that the pause holds
The contract's own Version detects the pause at the moment the save runs

choices: Creation also touches Country.Version, so the stale writer conflicts
The pause cancels in-flight creations by deleting their drafts
Creation re-reads the country inside a lock that the pause holds
The contract's own Version detects the pause at the moment the save runs

items.explanation: Lesson 3 lines 83-87: creation and activation touch Country.Version when saving and the pause changes the same country row, so a writer using a stale country version conflicts; Country is the common record on which the competing decisions meet. The stated tradeoff is that unrelated hiring operations in one country may conflict and need a reload. No lock or cancellation is involved, and a contract's own Version is not the row the pause changes.

items.prompt: A ClientAdmin key calls GET /api/contracts?clientId=<another client's id>. What does the code return?

choices.text: 200 and an empty array: both client filters are applied together
403, because the filter names a client it may not see
200 with its own contracts, and the clientId query value ignored
404, as for any other cross-client resource it asks for

choices: 200 and an empty array: both client filters are applied together
403, because the filter names a client it may not see
200 with its own contracts, and the clientId query value ignored
404, as for any other cross-client resource it asks for

items.explanation: Lines 27-36 add Where(ClientId == own) and then, when clientId is given, Where(ClientId == clientId); the two ANDed conditions match nothing, so the page is empty. The ADR wording and the comment ("whatever filter they pass") read as if the filter were ignored, but the code does not ignore it. Lists never 403 or 404 by ownership.
